prompt.context: Our client is a US defense contractor and one of its divisions manufactures attack helicopters for military operations. The company is considering setting up a new plant to meet increasing demand in the attack helicopter space. These helicopters are fully equipped with guns and ammo when delivered to the end customer. Our client has considered three sites to setup operations: Brazil, France, and the US.
prompt.question: How would you make this decision, and where should our client set up the plant based on that analysis?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current capacity situation at existing US plants?
clarifying_info.a: Our client has 3 plants in the US: 2 in Kansas and 1 in Michigan. The plants operate at full capacity today. One of the US plants can accommodate an additional assembly line at a cost of $500M; the other 2 are landlocked in residential areas and cannot be expanded.

framework: Profitability Analysis of Each Site: compare fixed costs, variable costs, initial setup costs, and revenues across US, Brazil, and France over the planning horizon
Logistics: what does it take to get the product to the customer — labor availability, skilled managers and technicians, export control restrictions
Suppliers: adequacy of supply base in each location — assembly inputs, spare parts, raw materials, ability to import what is needed under local regulations

Customers: where customers are based, need to be close to customer for design inputs, government preference for domestic suppliers, custom vs. standard designs, proprietary information considerations, private security market potential

questions.prompt: Walk through the financial analysis. Calculate 5-year profit for a plant in the US vs. Brazil. (France can be dismissed once costs and export restrictions are noted.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize France has the same export restriction as the US (no exports allowed) but higher costs than the US and lower revenues than Brazil, making it dominated. For US: revenues come only from the US market due to export restrictions. For Brazil: revenues come from both US and Brazil markets; helicopters imported into the US require a $15M/unit certification; manufacturing variable cost in Brazil is $20M/unit. Candidate should label footnotes clearly — VC for Brazil-built copters sold to the US includes both the $20M manufacturing VC and the $15M certification, totaling $35M/unit for US-bound units from Brazil.

math.setup: Evaluate 5-year profit = Revenue – Variable Cost – Fixed Cost – Initial Setup Cost for US and Brazil plants. Revenue = (defense budget) × (% allocated to client helicopters). # of helicopters = Revenue / $100M selling price.
steps: US plant: Revenue = 20% × $100B = $20B. # of helicopters = $20B / $100M = 200. VC = 200 × $15M = $3B. FC = $100M/yr × 5 = $500M. Initial cost = $500M. Profit = $20B – $3B – $500M – $500M = $16B

Brazil plant: US revenue = 20% × $100B = $20B → 200 helicopters to US (certification cost $15M/unit included in VC). BR revenue = 50% × $15B = $7.5B → 75 helicopters to BR. VC = (275 helicopters × $20M manufacturing) + (200 helicopters × $15M certification) = $5.5B + $3B = $8.5B. FC = $100M/yr × 5 = $500M. Initial cost = $2B. Total revenue = $20B + $7.5B = $27.5B. Total costs = $8.5B + $500M + $2B = $11B. Profit = $27.5B – $11B = $16.5B
France plant: same export restriction as US (no exports), higher VC ($25M) and higher setup cost ($3B) than US — clearly dominated; can be dismissed without full calculation.
Key takeaway: Brazil plant yields $16.5B profit vs. $16B for US plant — $500M higher over 5 years.
math.answer: Brazil plant profit = $16.5B; US plant profit = $16B. Brazil is more profitable by $500M over 5 years.

questions.prompt: What are the potential risks of manufacturing helicopters in Brazil?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify: political stability risk in Brazil, product quality concerns when operating farther from headquarters, robustness of the Brazilian supply chain, cultural differences affecting business relationships, national security concerns (defense equipment manufactured outside the US), brand image and trust considerations, and potential lack of know-how in a new country.

brainstorming.prompt: Evaluate the potential risks of acquiring (manufacturing) helicopters in Brazil.

categories.name: Political & Regulatory
ideas: Political instability in Brazil could disrupt operations
Export control policies between US and Brazil may shift over 5-year horizon
National security concerns — defense equipment manufactured outside the US

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Robustness of supply chain in Brazil
Product quality control farther from headquarters
Lack of know-how in a new country

categories.name: Commercial & Cultural
ideas: Cultural customs differ and may affect business relationships
Brand image and trust in helicopters built in Brazil
Customer (US government) comfort with foreign-manufactured defense assets

recommendation: Based on the 5-year financial analysis, Brazil is the recommended site for the new plant
Brazil yields $500M higher profit than a US expansion and significantly outperforms France
Brazil also reduces dependence on a single country (US) for sales, providing revenue diversification
risks: Political instability in Brazil and potential changes to favorable export control policies
National security concerns about manufacturing defense equipment outside the US
Supply chain robustness and product quality control in a new operating environment
Cultural differences potentially complicating business relationships
next_steps: Assess the global market opportunity — potential to sell to countries beyond the US and Brazil
Gauge labor reaction at existing US plants to a foreign expansion
Monitor US-Brazil diplomatic relations to ensure continued favorable export treatment
Conduct detailed supply chain due diligence in Brazil before committing capital
